subject: Nimbus POC: recommended model shortlist, benchmarks and regression notes
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cole <sara@nimblestack.io>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus demo recap + candidate shortlist and next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Appreciate the clear walkthrough of your ingestion patterns and the example API flows — that helped us prioritize the evaluation items. Recap + recommended next steps below.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Batch update ingestion (750–2k docs/day), majority short docs (~1–300 tokens) with a long-tail of longer clinical notes (1–5k tokens).
- Hard latency requirement for the clinical UI: p95 under 400ms for single-turn generation at ~128 tokens.
- High sensitivity to hallucination in clinical summarization; safety evaluation is required.
- Budget target (hosted) ~ $3k–$6k / month during POC.

Recommended shortlist (initial candidates we believe balance cost / latency / quality):
1) Redwood-7B-quant (4-bit) — Advantages: best cost profile, steady sub-200ms p50 latency on our Dedicated baseline. Good for rapid iteration.
   - Typical p50 / p95: 150ms / 320ms (128 tokens) on a single A10G-like instance; estimated hosted cost: ~$0.9k / month at POC volume.
2) Mistral-7B-v1 (fp16) — Advantages: higher raw quality on summarization tasks, balanced latency.
   - Typical p50 / p95: 210ms / 420ms; est hosted cost: ~$1.7k / month.
3) OpenLLaMA-13B-8bit — Advantages: best-quality candidate for edge clinical cases, but higher cost and p95 risk.
   - Typical p50 / p95: 420ms / 750ms; est hosted cost: ~$4.2k / month.

Why these three? They cover the sweet spots you described: a low-cost iterative model, a balanced quality/latency pick, and a high-quality fallback for sensitive notes. We recommend starting POC evals with Redwood-7B-quant and Mistral-7B in parallel and gating the 13B candidate behind targeted QA on hard prompt sets.

Attached I dropped a short benchmark summary, the prompt sets we used for the call, and a short eval note with observed failure modes. Link to the folder is below as well.

Action items proposed:
- Redwood: provision an evaluation API key + shared workspace and run the full prompt set overnight (we'll upload the prompt sets to your shared folder). (Action: Tessa) — ETA 48 hours.
- Nimble: confirm which clinical note templates you want prioritized (top 3). (Action: Sara) — ETA 48 hours.
- Pricing debounce: we will return POC pricing options for Hosted and Dedicated within the follow-up (Action: Michael) — ETA 2 business days.

Risks / regression notes:
- Quality drift: with quantized 4-bit runs we saw occasional tokenization-related artifacts on multi-paragraph summarization. We'll attach a small regression checklist and recommend automated nightly evals against your canonical set.
- Latency tail on occasional 13B spikes: we recommend soft fallback policy to Mistral-7B for p95 breaches to maintain UI SLOs.

Can we target a quick sync Friday (8/28) to review the first eval outputs and pick the pilot model for the UI integration? If another time works better, propose it and we'll adapt.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0128

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus demo recap + candidate shortlist and next steps

Thanks Tessa — this is super helpful. A few clarifying q's before we run the sets: 

1) For the Redwood-7B-quant: can you confirm whether hallucination rates were measured on the clinical summarization set (the one we reviewed)? If so, what metric did you use?
2) For the Mistral-7B estimate, the p95 is above our 400ms cutoff. Can you confirm the hardware assumptions and whether we can get p95 under 400ms with batching or a dedicated config?
3) On the OpenLLaMA-13B: we'd like to reserve it for a human-in-the-loop review — do you have a recommended evaluation plan for HITL specifically for hallucination checks?

Also — procurement asked for a simple summary line for cost vs impact to include in our sponsor email. Can you provide a single-paragraph recommended option (one sentence) to recommend to our Director?

Best,
Sara
Sara Cole
Head of Product | NimbleStack
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cole <sara@nimblestack.io>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimbus demo recap + candidate shortlist and next steps

Great questions — answers below, plus a short recommended line for your sponsor.

1) Hallucination measurement (Redwood-7B-quant):
   - Metric: fraction of summaries containing at least one verifiably incorrect fact vs the reference (we used a human-in-the-loop binning for ~200 samples, plus an automated NER-based contradiction detector). Observed ~6% failure rate on the clinical summarization set. Failures were mostly around improper date resolution and dropped negations in long notes.

2) Mistral-7B p95 and hardware:
   - Hardware assumption: single A10G-equivalent GPU, medium batching disabled for interactive flows. p95 can often be pushed below 400ms by: enabling a small (2–3 request) micro-batch within 25ms scheduling window and moving to a 2-GPU Dedicated pool for higher parallelism. We can provide a quick config that demonstrates p95 ~370ms. (Action: Michael to prototype).

3) OpenLLaMA-13B HITL plan:
   - Suggested plan: run 1k production-like prompts through the model, flag candidate outputs using an automated hallucination heuristic (NER contradiction + domain-specific regex checks), and route flagged outputs to clinicians for triage. Expected human review load: ~120–180 items for 1k prompts depending on thresholds. We'll include tooling to surface diffed revisions and source highlights.

Sponsor sentence (one-line recommend):
"Recommend Mistral-7B for the POC to balance accuracy and latency; fall back to Redwood-7B-quant for cost-focused tests and escalate to OpenLLaMA-13B for clinician-reviewed edge cases."

Next steps: we will provision the eval keys tonight and upload the full benchmark run to your folder; Michael will share the micro-batching config and expected p95 numbers by EOD Thursday.

Thanks —
Tessa
